<!-- Write for a reviewer who has not read the conversation. Use short, flat bullets and plain sentences, with one source line per paragraph. Aim for 100–200 words; simple changes can be shorter, and necessary evidence takes priority. Replace placeholders and omit optional bullets. -->

## Description

<!-- Lead with the problem and resulting behavior. Describe final scope and material risks, rather than chronology or a file inventory. Link the issue once when applicable; use Closes only when this PR completes all acceptance criteria. For partial or stacked PRs, include dependency PRs and remaining scope. -->

- <Problem and resulting behavior.>
- <Essential scope, constraint, or risk, if needed.>
- Refs #<issue>.

## Verification

<!-- State what actually ran and its result, preferably the user behavior or acceptance scenario checked. Include exact commands or reproduction/artifact links. State relevant checks not run and why; distinguish planned checks from passing results. -->

- `<command>`: <actual result and behavior checked>.

<!-- Keep review SHAs, bot activity, CI retry logs, and handoff details in the review record or handoff comment. Update stale text as scope changes. Remove empty sections, repeated rationale, and generic checklists. Before publishing, check scope, bullets, links, and verification; read back the saved GitHub body to verify formatting and content. -->
